guard_package_affected.reason: B1 changes no file under tools/guard, tools/guardpkg or tools/guardops; the active installation stays untouched.

plan_change.decided_by: commit plan rule for live-found functional defects
plan_change.reason: Mechanically traced before the first live start: frontend/src-tauri/src/lib.rs set OPENJARVIS_PERSONAL_ENABLED and PERSONAL_JARVIS_CONTACTS_SIDECAR but never PERSONAL_JARVIS_CALENDAR_SIDECAR, and the resolver accepts only explicitly injected paths (src/personaljarvis/base/sidecar/resolver.py). A packed app could enable the module yet never resolve its own bundled calendar bridge. Repaired as its own functional commit; no amend.

second_change.decided_by: commit plan rule for live-found functional defects
second_change.reason: Pre-live TCC identity check: frontend/src-tauri/Info.plist declared only NSContactsUsageDescription. Without NSCalendarsUsageDescription macOS denies or aborts instead of showing the dialog — from outside indistinguishable from a user's no (same failure class as the entitlement finding in docs/testing/calendar-read-probe-x86_64-2026-08-04.md). The texts are lifted from the sidecar's own Info.plist; the b1 bundle check now fails mechanically on a missing usage description. Own functional commit; no amend.

third_change.decided_by: commit plan rule for live-found functional defects (F1: blocks the visible goal)
third_change.reason: First real live run on 2026-08-08: the packed app started, the sidebar entry and the route worked, but the view showed 'Die Kalender-Bridge ist nicht verfuegbar' and offered no authorization button, so no TCC dialog could ever appear. Mechanically diagnosed against the running backend: GET /status returned bridge_available=false with detail 'noch nicht geprueft' — by contract it reports the LAST KNOWN state and never probes — while POST /bridge/check against the same backend returned bridge_available=true, authorization_status=not_determined. The sidecar path was correctly injected and resolvable; nothing was wrong with packaging. The view now runs the calendar-free handshake before it believes the status. Own functional commit; no amend.

planned_commits.message: feat(calendar): make the calendar reachable and packageable on x86_64
planned_commits.purpose: functional: the sidebar entry with its navigation test, the B1 gate scaffold (runner, manifest, lineage, this plan, live-record loader binding) — everything the visible x86_64 calendar goal needs and nothing else

planned_commits.message: fix(calendar): inject the bundled calendar sidecar path into the backend start
planned_commits.purpose: functional repair found while mechanically tracing the packed-app chain before the live run: the backend start injected only the contacts sidecar path; without PERSONAL_JARVIS_CALENDAR_SIDECAR the resolver (which accepts only injected paths) could never reach the bundled calendar bridge

planned_commits.message: fix(calendar): declare the calendar usage descriptions on the app bundle
planned_commits.purpose: functional repair found while mechanically preparing the TCC live run: the app Info.plist carried only the contacts usage description; without NSCalendarsUsageDescription macOS aborts instead of asking. The bundle check now catches this class mechanically

planned_commits.message: fix(calendar): probe the bridge before the view believes the last known status
planned_commits.purpose: functional repair found by the first real TCC live run: the view read only the deliberately last-known /status and therefore claimed a missing bridge on a fresh backend, hiding the authorization path; the calendar-free handshake now runs before the status is believed

planned_commits.message: test(calendar): finalize b1 visible-calendar evidence, acceptance and handoff
planned_commits.purpose: purely determinative: gate evidence of the five phases against the fixed functional commit and the live run, the PII-poor live record, the x86_64 K1 mapping, acceptance and handoff

condition_per_commit: the position is self contained: it introduces no reference to an artifact a later position creates
the configuration loader binding check passes
every phase declared for the changed subject has run against the new scope (R5)

a commit that introduces or changes a block manifest is green only when every phase that manifest declares has run against it, where phases requiring live interaction may be green from the acceptance run they describe
split_justification.context_rule: If the context runs short, work stops before the commit and reports, rather than leaving finished work unsecured or committing it unverified.
split_justification.reason: B1 stays deliberately small: one functional commit carries the visible goal, the determinative commit carries only evidence of the run against it. A genuine functional defect found by the live run creates a further functional commit with a machine-readable reason here, never an amend.
split_justification.separation: normative and determinative stay in separate branch commits; position 1 is functional, position 2 is determinative
